books.section: Unit 5: Toward the Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877)

stimulus.source_note: Treaty of December 30, 1853 (Gadsden Purchase), Article I, as ratified; Article III as ratified set the payment at $10 million. Public domain.
stimulus.text:
Article I. The Mexican Republic agrees to designate the following as her true limits with the United States for the future: . . . Beginning in the Gulf of Mexico, three leagues from land, opposite the mouth of the Rio Grande, as provided in the 5th article of the treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo; thence, as defined in the said article, up the middle of that river to the point where the parallel of 31° 47′ north latitude crosses the same; thence due west one hundred miles; thence south to the parallel of 31° 20′ north latitude; thence along the said parallel of 31° 20′ to the 111th meridian of longitude west of Greenwich; thence in a straight line to a point on the Colorado River twenty English miles below the junction of the Gila and Colorado rivers . . .

[Article III, as ratified, set the payment to Mexico at $10 million.]

source: original; stimulus as noted in stimulus.source_note
stem: The Gadsden Purchase of 1853 is best remembered as which of the following?

options.text: The last land added to the continental United States.
The first land the United States bought from France.
options.misconception: The Louisiana Purchase of 1803 was the land bought from France, fifty years earlier.

options.text: The purchase that gave the United States the Oregon Territory.
options.misconception: Oregon came by treaty with Britain in 1846, not by purchase from Mexico.

options.text: The deal that admitted Texas as a slave state.
options.misconception: Texas was annexed in 1845, eight years before the Gadsden Purchase.

rationales.A: No land has been added to the continental United States since the Gadsden strip in 1853.
rationales.B: The land from France was the Louisiana Purchase of 1803.
rationales.C: Oregon was settled with Britain in 1846; the Gadsden strip lay on the Mexican border.
rationales.D: Texas joined the Union in 1845; the Gadsden Purchase came in 1853.
rationales.general:
1. Place the purchase on the map: a strip along today's southern Arizona and New Mexico.
2. Ask what came after it. Nothing — no further land was added to the continental United States.
3. That is its fame. The purchase drew the last line of the map of the lower forty-eight states.
Remember: the Gadsden strip finished the map — after 1853, the continental United States had the shape it keeps today.
